chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who married his male slave to his own umm al-wald (mother of a child) slave, and she had not borne him a child from the master, then the master died. He said: 'She has no option (of choosing to stay with or leave the slave); she is owned by the heirs.'

key_terms.أُمِّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-wald: A female slave who bears a child to her master

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an umm al-wald who is married to a slave if she hasn't borne a child from her master?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the 'umm al-wald' status is contingent upon bearing a child specifically by the master; since she bore no offspring from him, her emancipation is not triggered upon his death. Consequently, she remains a slave property to be distributed among the heirs, illustrating the precise conditions under which concubines transition from servitude to freedom in Shia jurisprudence.
